Conditional on severe disruption and traffic falling from about 25 to 10 daily IMF-reported transits, with a narrower provider subsequently reporting four crossings, the chance becomes materially higher. If traffic stayed near ten daily with independent arrivals, a zero day would remain very unlikely; clustered shipping, further attacks and temporary coordinated suspensions make that simple model unreliable. Over the remaining ten days, a zero day is a substantial minority possibility. The supplied evidence does not support a measured historical frequency.
out.key_uncertainty: Whether disruption intensifies enough to stop even the residual Iranian-route traffic for an entire PortWatch reporting day, and how PortWatch coverage and daily boundaries translate sparse actual crossings into published counts. Missing individual IMF daily values also leave a possibility of an already-occurring but unestablished zero day; the latest IMF-based evidence extends only through July 19. Continued residual traffic supports NO, while the sharp decline and attacks support a meaningful chance of a temporary zero.
